⚙ Settings
🔒 Privacy & data flow
Everything runs in this browser — there is no Evidentum server. Tap for exactly what leaves your browser, and when.
Your projects, screening decisions, notes and API keys are stored locally in this browser (localStorage / IndexedDB) and are never uploaded by the app. Data leaves your browser only when you act:
  • Searching sends your query to each database you tick — PubMed/NCBI, Europe PMC, Cochrane, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Scopus/Elsevier, ClinicalTrials.gov — directly to that provider’s API.
  • AI appraisal sends the paper’s title/abstract (and fetched full text) plus the prompt to whichever AI provider’s key you entered (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI). It runs only when you start it, and is billed to your key.
  • Semantic Scholar may retry through a public CORS proxy if the direct call is blocked — then your search terms pass through the proxy operator (see the Semantic Scholar section below). No other database search uses a proxy.
  • Full-text PDF retrieval requests a paper’s PDF directly from its host. Only if that is blocked and you opt in (Full-text PDF retrieval section) does it retry via a public proxy, which then sees the full PDF URL; a signed / credential-bearing link is never proxied. Off by default.
  • API keys are saved in this browser (localStorage by default; browser extensions or scripts running on this page could read them). Untick “Remember keys on this device” in the AI keys section to keep them for the current tab only — cleared when you close it. Backups exclude keys unless you opt in.
AI output is an advisory draft for a human reviewer to verify — never a final eligibility or risk-of-bias judgement.

📚 LibKey — Institutional Library Access
One-click full-text access via your institution. Find your ID at libkey.io
📄 Full-text PDF retrieval
🔒 Privacy note: When Evidentum reads a paper’s full text for appraisal it requests the PDF directly from its host. If your browser blocks that (CORS) and you tick this box, it retries through a public CORS proxy (allorigins / codetabs) — which means the complete PDF URL is sent to the proxy operator. With the box unticked (the default) a blocked PDF is simply skipped and reported, with no third party in the path. To protect your access, a signed or credential-bearing PDF link (one carrying an access token, signature or institutional-resolver key) is never routed through a proxy even when this is on.
👓 Scopus API Credentials Optional
Free for academic use. Register at dev.elsevier.com · InstToken needed for off-campus access · Enable the Scopus chip on the search tab once keys are entered.
🔬 NCBI / PubMed API Key Optional
Raises PubMed's rate limit from 3 to 10 requests/sec — recommended for large searches (e.g. 500/DB). Free from your NCBI account → Settings → API Key Management. Searches still work without it, just slower.
🧠 Semantic Scholar API Key Optional
A free key moves Semantic Scholar off the shared anonymous rate-limit pool (fewer “rate limited” errors) — request one at semanticscholar.org/product/api. The biomedical-fields limit raises precision but can reduce recall (S2's field tags are imperfect), so leave it off for an exhaustive search and on to cut off-topic noise.
🔒 Privacy note: Semantic Scholar usually works with a direct request. Rarely, a browser blocks it (CORS); only then, and only if you tick the box above, Evidentum retries through a public CORS proxy (allorigins / codetabs) — and the full request URL, including your search terms, passes through the proxy operator. With the box unticked (the default) a blocked Semantic Scholar request simply fails and is reported, with no third party in the path. Every other database always talks directly to its API; the desktop build never uses a proxy.
🔑 Saved credentials
All the keys above are stored in this browser only. Wipe every one of them — AI provider keys plus Scopus, NCBI and Semantic Scholar — in a single step. Your projects and screening data are not affected.
🌍 Europe PMC Free · no key
Europe PMC's synonym=true auto-adds controlled-vocabulary synonyms (e.g. “heart attack” also matches “myocardial infarction”) — a strong recall boost but a large precision hit (result counts can jump >10×). Leave off for a precise search; turn on to maximise sensitivity. Deep results now page through all matches (cursorMark) instead of stopping at the first 1,000.
📏 Phrase Proximity Advanced
Matches multi-word phrases when the words appear within N words of each other, instead of exactly adjacent — wider recall than an exact phrase, far tighter than a loose AND. Applied to the PubMed ([tiab:~N]), Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar ("…"~N) queries; Scopus / OpenAlex / ClinicalTrials keep exact phrases (no native proximity operator).
💾 Backup & Restore
Your projects, screened papers and screening decisions are stored in this browser only — they're lost if you clear browsing data or switch device. Export a full backup regularly (and before any clean-up), then restore it anywhere. API keys are never included.
💾 Assessment Memory
AI appraisals are saved locally (by DOI/PMID) so a paper is never re-assessed — or re-billed — across searches. Export a portable pack to back it up, move it to another device, or share it.

📚 References, Licences & Copyright
Appraisal tools & reporting guidelines — citations & licences
Evidentum is a free, non-commercial research tool. The reporting guidelines and risk-of-bias / quality-appraisal instruments below are reproduced for use within the app with attribution to their authors. Items under a NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence are reproduced verbatim (signalling questions unaltered) and used only because this tool is non-commercial. Always consult the original source for full guidance.
Using papers responsibly — copyright & the PDF uploader

The articles you search, link to, or upload remain the copyright of their publishers and authors. Evidentum grants you no rights over them — it only helps you find, read and appraise material you are already entitled to access. You are responsible for using each paper within its licence.

✓ Open Access — fine to analyse with AI

When a free / OA full text is found (the green ◆ OA full text badge on a result), AI agent analysis may appraise the whole paper. OA licences (e.g. CC‑BY) explicitly permit reuse and text-and-data mining.

⚠ Subscription / paywalled — read it yourself, don't auto-feed it

An institutional subscription is a personal-use licence: it lets you read the article, via the 📚 Library Access (LibKey) link. Evidentum will not automatically send paywalled text to an AI provider, and you should not bulk-upload subscription PDFs into an automated pipeline — systematic downloading breaches most publisher agreements and can suspend your whole institution's access.

📋 The PDF uploader — what's OK to upload

Only upload a PDF you have lawfully obtained and may use for your own research — your own manuscript, an Open Access article, or a paper you accessed through your institution's subscription for personal study. An uploaded PDF is processed in your browser; its text is sent only to your chosen AI provider for that single appraisal. Evidentum has no server and never stores or forwards it anywhere else.

🤖 Where the text goes

Any full text or abstract you appraise is sent directly to the AI provider you selected (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or xAI Grok) under their API and data-handling terms. Review your provider's data-use and retention policy before sending third-party copyrighted content.

This is practical guidance, not legal advice. When in doubt about a specific article or publisher, check with your institution's library or copyright office.

Define your question (PICO)
Enter your research question in PICO terms. The assistant drafts concept blocks and search terms; you edit, restructure, and approve every part. Live result counts come from PubMed’s server — never from the AI.

2
Concept blocks — edit freely
Each block is one concept; terms within a block are combined with OR. Concepts are combined with AND — except the intervention & comparator, which are OR-combined (either arm) by default, and the outcome, which is left out of the search unless you tick it (per Cochrane). Add or remove terms and blocks; click a term to delete it. MeSH terms are tagged MeSH; free-text tiab.
💬 Methodology notes — the model’s critique of its own draft
3
Assembled PubMed strategy & live count
Numbered search sets (PRESS / PRISMA-S — for your methods section)
Paywalled databases — copy & paste (Ovid Embase · Cochrane CENTRAL · Web of Science)
These databases are subscription-only, with no public search API, so Evidentum cannot search them for you: paste the translated strategy into your institution’s own interface, run it there, then bring the records back with ↓ Import records on the Results tab (choose the matching source) so they join the pool with full deduplication and PRISMA provenance. ⚠️ Ovid Embase: subject headings are translated mechanically from MeSH — verify each exp …/ line against Emtree (Embase’s own thesaurus) and remap where the vocabularies differ. CENTRAL indexes MeSH natively so headings carry over as-is; no RCT filter line is added because CENTRAL is already a register of controlled trials. Web of Science indexes no subject vocabulary at all, so every heading becomes a free-text topic phrase searched as an exact phrase — read it for missing word variants.
Ovid · Embase (Advanced Search)
Cochrane Library · CENTRAL (Search Manager)
Web of Science · Core Collection (Advanced Search)
ℹ️ This PubMed strategy is translated to each database’s native syntax when you send it to the workbench. MeSH headings only search as MeSH in PubMed (and, partially, Europe PMC) — Scopus, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and ClinicalTrials.gov search them as free-text keywords, so every concept needs free-text synonyms to travel. Inverted headings (e.g. “Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2”) are auto-rewritten to natural word order for those engines.
The count is the true number of PubMed records this strategy retrieves (NCBI History server). Aim for a manageable, comprehensive set — the coach above suggests adjustments.
🎯 Known-item recall check (optional but recommended)
Paste PMIDs or DOIs of papers you already know belong in this review. If the strategy misses any, it isn’t sensitive enough — widen the terms and re-check. The date filter is ignored here (concept terms + study-design only).

Database Query
Search in:
📚 Cochrane Reviews searches Europe PMC filtered to the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews journal. It is driven by your primary (MeSH) query and merged/deduplicated with other sources.
👓 Scopus needs an Elsevier API key, entered in Settings (⚙ top right). Get one free at dev.elsevier.com.

The key works on your institution's network. Off-campus, you also need an InstToken — request one from Elsevier API Support using your institutional email.
🧪 ClinicalTrials.gov searches the AACT (Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov) public API for registered and unpublished clinical trials. Results include ongoing, completed, and terminated trials that may not yet appear in PubMed. Useful for identifying grey literature and publication bias. No API key required.
ℹ️ Two-stream search. The primary bar takes your full PubMed MeSH/boolean strategy and drives the MEDLINE-indexed sources (PubMed, Europe PMC, Cochrane). The secondary bar is auto-derived as a plain-keyword version (MeSH tags stripped) for the natural-language engines that don't understand MeSH. Edit the secondary freely — it won't be overwritten unless you click Re-derive.
🔬 Primary search — PubMed / MEDLINE (MeSH & boolean) source of truth · drives PubMed, Europe PMC, Cochrane
💡 Plain keywords work fine — use "quotes" for exact phrases and AND / OR to combine ideas. This one query searches every ticked database at once, and duplicates are removed automatically.

2
Keyword triage signals
— a reading-order aid, applied to each title & abstract after retrieval
Each signal scans the title and abstract for your keywords. Must contain = flagged ✓ if any keyword is found. Must NOT contain = flagged ✓ if no keyword is found (e.g. "animal, rat, mouse" to down-rank animal studies). More signals detected ranks a paper higher for triage. Keywords match at the start of a word (like a database * truncation), so "randomis" catches "randomised" and "randomisation" but "male" won't match "female". These are simple text matches to help you decide what to read first — they do not determine eligibility, study quality or risk of bias. Edit the signals in the table below.
Criterion Label Keywords (comma-separated, case-insensitive) Rule type
3
Automated Quality Checklists
— run automatically on any paper with full text available
Once a paper's full text is retrieved (via PubMed Central or a free PDF), the app will automatically run quality checklists against the text. Each checklist item is keyword-scanned and pre-filled as a starting point — you can review and adjust each item manually inside the paper's expanded view. Checklists are matched to study type by default but can be changed per paper. The appropriate risk of bias tool is automatically selected and assessed alongside the matched quality checklist (e.g. RoB 2 for RCTs, ROBINS-I V2 for non-randomised intervention studies, Newcastle-Ottawa for cohort/case-control studies).
✓ CONSORT 2025 — RCTs ✓ PRISMA 2020 — Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses ✓ STROBE — Observational Studies ✓ CARE 2013 — Case Reports ✓ AGREE II — Clinical Guidelines ⚖ RoB 2 — RCT bias ⚖ ROBINS-I V2 — Non-randomised bias ⚖ Newcastle-Ottawa — Cohort/Case-Control ⚖ Jadad — RCT quality score

🤖 In-depth Analysis Running
⚡ Quick scan
The quick scan reads each record’s title and abstract (no full text), ranks its relevance to your question, and tags the study design where identifiable — cards sort into relevant / unclear / off-topic sections with a 0–100 score and a one-line reason. Nothing is removed automatically: tick the records you want out, then Remove selected. Fast and cheap — it judges relevance only, not study quality (that’s the in-depth analysis).
